title: Warmer Colours Only
tests: Tests interpreting 'warmer' as a colour-temperature adjustment rather than a scene or weather change.

faults.what: Fine textures in the trees, shoreline and water appear sharpened or enhanced rather than strictly preserving the source's softer detail.

judge.summary: The scene is convincingly warmer and retains its composition and reflections, though some fine detail appears enhanced beyond a colour-only edit.

must_haves.item: The image has a visibly warmer colour balance than the source.
must_haves.why: The sky and reflected light are more golden, and the trees have warmer olive tones.

must_haves.item: The same mountains, pine trees, clouds and lake remain in their original positions.
must_haves.why: The major landscape features and cloud shapes remain aligned with the source.

must_haves.item: The lake's reflections and surface details retain their original structure.
must_haves.why: The reflected mountains, clouds and trees retain their arrangement, along with the main ripple patterns.

must_haves.item: No sun, sunset, extra clouds or other scene elements are added.
must_haves.why: The warmer light comes from colour changes; no new scene elements are visible.

must_haves.item: Framing, geometry and image detail remain unchanged apart from colour.
must_haves.why: Framing and overall geometry are preserved, but fine foliage, shoreline and water textures look sharper than in the source.
